name: Lazarus BioRelief NociGuard Pain Modulator
body_location: spinal — epidural microarray implanted at the dorsal horn of the spinal cord, level determined by pain source; cranial adjunct node optional at thalamic pain-processing centers
description:
The Lazarus BioRelief NociGuard is a targeted nociceptive modulation implant designed for individuals managing chronic pain conditions — neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia-spectrum disorders, post-surgical pain syndromes, degenerative joint disease, and occupational overuse injuries among them. A flexible microelectrode array is implanted epidurally at the dorsal horn of the spinal cord at the dermatome level corresponding to the patient's primary pain region, where it intercepts afferent pain signals before they ascend to supraspinal processing centers. The array delivers precisely calibrated spinal cord stimulation pulses — low-frequency for background chronic pain suppression, with an adaptive burst-mode that activates in response to acute pain spikes detected by the system's onboard signal-pattern recognition. An optional thalamic adjunct node, implanted in a separate procedure, adds central pain-processing modulation for patients with widespread or centrally sensitized pain conditions. The system does not eliminate all sensation; it specifically targets the nociceptive signal pathway while preserving proprioception, pressure sensitivity, and temperature awareness. Lazarus BioRelief positions the NociGuard explicitly as a quality-of-life restoration device rather than a pain elimination tool, a distinction that matters both clinically and legally.

Chronic pain is one of the most quietly devastating conditions in GLMZ. On the Shelf and in Tier 2 industrial districts, bodies are worn down by physical labor, inadequate healthcare access, and the accumulated injuries of work that doesn't allow for recovery. By their forties, a significant portion of the working population carries some form of persistent pain, often managed through pharmaceutical means that carry their own costs and dependencies. The NociGuard represents a different approach: not a drug that must be continuously purchased and that the body will eventually resist, but a device that modulates the pain signal itself. For many users, the experience of installation is described with words that feel disproportionate to the clinical description — people say they got their life back, that they had forgotten what it felt like to exist in their body without the constant background noise of pain. Lazarus BioRelief offers the NociGuard through both licensed medical clinics and, in a controversial partnership with the city health bureau, through a subsidized program for workers in registered high-injury occupations.
installation_requirements: Licensed spinal intervention clinic; epidural implantation under local anesthesia with fluoroscopic guidance, 1.5–2 hours; requires pain medicine specialist or neurosurgical nurse practitioner; optional thalamic adjunct is a separate outpatient procedure requiring a neurotechnology clinic
maintenance: Biannual stimulation parameter review and adjustment at licensed clinic (can be done remotely for stable patients via Lazarus BioRelief telemetry system); battery replacement every 7 years (outpatient procedure); array integrity check annually

side_effects: Paresthesia — a mild tingling or buzzing sensation in the implant's coverage area — during the first several weeks as the body adapts to stimulation; usually described as more noticeable than unpleasant
Occasional sensation of heaviness or numbness in the lower extremities if stimulation parameters drift above optimal; corrected by recalibration

Small number of users report a period of emotional adjustment after pain relief is achieved, sometimes described as grief or disorientation at the absence of a sensation that had defined daily life for years
Rare: lead migration requiring minor repositioning procedure, most common in the first 6 months
cultural_context: In GLMZ, chronic pain is so normalized in working-class communities that people who don't have it are sometimes viewed with mild suspicion, as if they haven't worked hard enough or haven't lived enough life to acquire the wear. The NociGuard therefore occupies a complicated cultural position: it is deeply welcomed and deeply meaningful to those who receive it, but it also quietly challenges the stoic acceptance of pain that many communities have built identity around. On the Shelf, there is a generation of older residents who refused the NociGuard for years before finally relenting — not because of cost alone, but because managing pain had become part of how they understood themselves. Younger residents tend to have no such ambivalence. In Tier 3 and above, the NociGuard is framed entirely as a medical device and carries no stigma whatsoever; if anything, it is a marker of pragmatic self-care. The Lazarus brand carries weight across all tiers — it is one of the older and more trusted names in implant medicine, and the BioRelief subsidiary has carefully cultivated a reputation for patient-centered design rather than feature maximalism.
known_users: Industrial and construction workers with occupational overuse injuries and degenerative joint conditions
Older Tier 1 and 2 residents managing lifetimes of accumulated physical damage
People with neuropathic pain conditions, fibromyalgia-spectrum disorders, or post-surgical pain syndromes
Tier 3 and 4 individuals with chronic migraines or centrally sensitized pain conditions
Workers in Lazarus BioRelief's city bureau subsidized high-injury occupation program
story_hooks: A labor organizer who has been a vocal critic of a major manufacturing corponation is found dead, and her NociGuard's stimulation logs show that her pain management was remotely escalated — not suppressed — in the hours before her death, suggesting someone with access to the Lazarus telemetry system wanted her incapacitated.

A group of NociGuard users in a Tier 1 district are all experiencing sudden, complete pain suppression far beyond their prescribed parameters — no tingling, no awareness of injury at all. They're hurting themselves without knowing it. The firmware update that caused it was pushed three days ago.

The city health bureau's subsidized NociGuard program is being quietly discontinued for workers in one specific occupation: waste processing. The players are asked to find out whether the decision is budgetary, political, or something more specific to what those workers are exposed to.
